newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil real ends off 0.06 pct as mini-band lowered.
newsitem.headline: Brazil real ends off 0.06 pct as mini-band lowered.

text.p: Brazil's real fell 0.06 percent to close at 1.0326 per dollar in the commercial foreign exchange market after the Central Bank surprised the market by setting a weaker mini-band for the currency, dealers said.
The Central Bank set the new trading level for the fluctuation of the real by buying dollars at 1.0325 reais and selling at 1.0375 in an early morning auction.
"We were expecting a drop in the mini-band on Friday, but not today," one trader said.
The previous mini-band was set on Tuesday between 1.0315 and 1.0365 reais to the dollar.
The market was also surprised because the Central Bank lowered the mini-band 0.1 percent and not 0.05 percent as banks had expected.

After today's action, dealers do not expect another drop in the mini-band on Friday, even though the Central Bank has been lowering it on the last trading session of the month for the past few months.
"The Central Bank has lowered the mini-band 0.6 percent so far this month and the market would be very surprised if it does anything else on Friday," one dealer said.
In the interbank floating rate market, the real fell 0.1 percent to end at 1.0382 to the dollar, following the drop in the mini-band.
In the illegal parallel market, the real closed at 1.10 per greenback, down 0.18 percent, traders said.
